reason: The only Casper (C03) is noted as 'sr, sv Jan', but the genealogy gives this man's father as Casper (Jeremias). That parentage conflict points to a different Casper, possibly his father.
No owner is named Willem Jacobus. C07 Willem Christoffel has a different second name and is noted 'sv Corn.', which contradicts the genealogy father Gerhardus sr.
The only candidate, Godlieb Rudolph, is a clearly different given name from Daniël Jacobus.
The genealogy records only 'Jacobus', and C03 Jacobus Theodorus in Uitenhage shares that first name and the district. An omitted middle name is normal, whereas C01 has Jacobus only as a second name.
C02 Hendrik Jacobus De Bruyn in Somerset exactly matches the full name and the declared district.
Neither Gysbert Sybrand nor Johannes Gerhardus Stephanus matches Hendrik Lambert. C01's note 'sv Gysbert' also conflicts with the father Johannes Jacob.
The only candidate, Jan Lodewyk, is a clearly different given name from Frederik Andries.
Johan Hendrik differs from Johannes Jacob in the second name. A shared first name alone is weak, and no other evidence links them.
C06 'Pieter, sr; sv Jan' in Somerset exactly matches the single given name Pieter and the declared district. 'Sr' fits a man already married in 1820, and no father is recorded to contradict 'sv Jan'.
C04 Arnoldus Jacobus Greyling exactly matches the full name, and Somerset was formerly part of Cradock, which fits the declared district.
